text:
alana: quick flag  hitting an odd SSE resume/dedup case in the new samples. When a proxy coalesces two events into a single TCP/HTTP2 frame and the client aborts mid-read, on reconnect with Last-Event-ID we occasionally see the previous token replay.
diego: can you paste a minimal capture? which SDKs are affected?
alana: Node + Browser + Go samples. Capture shows server emitted:
id: 321
data: {"tok":"one"}

id: 322
data: {"tok":"two"}

Proxy coalesced writes so the client read returned one buffer: `data:{"tok":"one"}
data:{"tok":"two"}
` (single trailing blank line). Then client aborts for an auth refresh and reconnects with Last-Event-ID:321. Server resends 321 and the SDK delivers "one" again -> duplicate.
harper: classic boundary collapse. TCP/TLS/HTTP2 do not preserve application write boundaries. We should never design against chunk boundaries.
diego: today our Node sample uses a naive split on "\n\n" which explains the sensitivity. Go SDK has an eventsource parser that tolerates single-LF; Node and Browser behave differently.
infra-bot: alert: small increase in SSE reconnects for streams in staging 2026-05-02T16:12:00Z :warning:
harper: two fixes for parity/DX: (1) SDK-level id dedupe across reconnects (keep small bounded set of recent ids), (2) optional lenient parse mode which will flush events on single-LF after a short configurable timeout so we don't block forever waiting for an extra blank line. Make both opt-in to avoid breaking strict users.
diego: implementation note: dedupe needs to be memory-safe for long-lived streams. Use ring buffer or LRU with TTL. Default capacity 1024, TTL 5m? Configurable. Emit metric `sse.dedup.skipped`.
alana: also need to expose `event.id` in the emitted event object so apps can opt-in to their own dedupe too. Some customers have server-side resume logic that depends on seeing raw ids.
harper: parser behaviour: default keep strict semantics. Add `sse.lenientFlushMs` default 0. If >0 and parser sees a single LF where a double LF was expected, start a timer; when timer fires emit what we have unless more bytes arrived. Small default like 30-50ms reduces delivery latency without changing strict behavior for users who prefer it.
diego: add integration tests: docker-compose with nginx/haproxy configured to merge writes and to split mid-json; test harness should script client aborts and reconnects with Last-Event-ID and assert no duplicates when dedupe enabled and lenientFlushMs set.
ci-bot: CI note: integration tests with nginx will add runtime. Suggest add them under an "integration-slow" job initially and gate later if stable.
docs-bot: docs note: add a short troubleshooting section in quickstart about "duplicate tokens on resume" describing middlebox buffering, how to enable server-side immediate flush, and SDK toggles `sse.dedupeById` and `sse.lenientFlushMs`. Include a minimal nginx config to reproduce.
alana: short-term workaround for users: include an increasing `seq` field in the event payload and dedupe at application layer until SDK fix lands. Also recommend server flush when possible.
harper: edge case: auth refresh flow sometimes cancels sockets mid-read. If auth refresh happens right after a merged read, we might still be racing. Consider making auth refresh attempt to drain outstanding bytes or delay abort a few ms if we just observed a read (heuristic). But that's complex and brittle. Dedupe + lenient flush is simpler and safer.
diego: action items:
- diego: open SDK issues for Node/Go/Browser to add `sse.dedupeById` + `sse.lenientFlushMs` with unit+integration tests
- harper: build docker-compose test harness (nginx/haproxy + tiny stream server + client scripts) and add to integration-slow CI
- alana: add example in examples/stream-resume showing how to reproduce with nginx + curl and a docs blurb on Last-Event-ID semantics
- infra-bot: scan ingress/router configs for `proxy_buffering`/buffering settings and report any non-defaults that could coalesce SSE writes

docs-bot: I'll draft the quick docs snippet and link an nginx reproducible conf.
diego: once PRs land add an E2E that simulates abort+reconnect asserting no duplicate logical tokens when `sse.dedupeById=true`. That should prevent regressions and reduce onboarding flakes.
alana: PR incoming for a minimal nginx repro and a tiny sample app. Will paste links when ready. :thumbsup:
